class_id: shared config not shipped by the code deploy
feature: scripts/deploy-linux.sh (shared/config symlink) + scripts/ops/deploy-config.sh + any schema-validated config file
symptom: a config file inside a release is a SYMLINK to a shared, slot-scoped file that the code deploy deliberately never overwrites (the same pattern as shared/env and shared/certs). A commit that tightens the config SCHEMA and updates the repo's copy of the config in the SAME change therefore ships the new validator against the OLD config, because only a separate manual command replaces the shared file. The loader refuses at process start and the service is dead — silently, because the deploy's own gate checks served sha, migrations and row counts, none of which require the service to start. Universal shape: any config whose validator ships on the code path while its VALUE ships on a different path can be broken by a single commit that touches both, and no CI drift check catches it because the repo copy is self-consistent.
first_seen: 2026-09-19 — `b5614cc7` (#781) added `comparisonFamily` as a required zod enum in `scraper/src/config/field-manifest-schema.ts` AND to `scraper/config/field-manifest.json`. Staging deployed `b12c9d28` at 07:58 IST; the shared manifest was still the 2026-09-18 03:41Z copy from `9c20b4d0`, which lacked the key. Every one of the 190 fields failed validation; the scraper crashed at start in 4-6s and every 30-min cycle failed (02:33:51Z, 02:45:01Z) until the shared file was deployed at 08:26 IST. Prod unaffected (older code, no shared-config symlink)
fix_prs: immediate recovery: `scripts/ops/deploy-config.sh --slot staging --sha b12c9d28` (verified: CONFIG_SHA updated, 190/190 fields carrying comparisonFamily). Open: #793 for the three mechanisms — (1) validate the DEPLOYED config against the DEPLOYED schema as a deploy gate and fail the deploy if the loader refuses, (2) a same-day consumer for `wake-failed ... exit=1` in the wake log, (3) alert on `shared/config/<slot>/CONFIG_SHA` drifting from the served sha, mirroring the existing deploy-drift-monitor
detection_check: THREE mechanisms, #793. (1) DEPLOY GATE (primary) - preflight_deployed_config() in scripts/deploy-linux.sh runs scraper/src/scripts/validate-deployed-config.ts BEFORE the atomic pointer flip and before SCRAPER_RESUME_TARGET="new", so a refusal is a genuine no-op: current still points at the last good release and the EXIT trap restores it. It loads the DEPLOYED field manifest through the scrapers OWN loader (loadFieldManifest, the code that crashed), and ONLY that file - the other scraper/config/*.json are not config-deployed and are flag-gated no-ops at runtime, so validating them would make the gate stricter than the process it models. Self-test scripts/tests/deploy-linux-config-preflight.test.sh: case 2 reproduces the incident (190 fields), case 5 is mutation-tested (moving the gate back after the flip turns it red), case 6 pins the file set. (2) LINEAGE CHECK OUTSIDE THE PROCESS - scripts/ops/config-lineage.mjs compares the served sha against shared/config/<slot>/CONFIG_SHA over read-only ssh. It exists BECAUSE the in-cycle copy cannot cover this incident: checkConfigLineage runs from runStep inside main(), and main() (index.ts:1651) is reached only AFTER the startup config validators (1646-1650) that throw during the failure - a detector killed by the failure it detects. CONFIG_SHA=="release" is reported UNKNOWN, never in-sync: deploy-linux.sh writes that marker only in its first-seed branch and no later deploy rewrites it, so a slot seeded once reads "release" forever while its shared manifest stays at day-1 content - the most drift-prone state, not the safest. Self-test scripts/tests/config-lineage.test.mjs. (3) WAKE-LOG CONSUMER - scripts/ops/wake-delta.mjs resolves wake-failed/ceiling-tripped lines to identities with NEW/GONE/SAME diffing and exit 3 on any class with no issue number (signal-ownership R1/R3); 18 such lines sat unread during the outage. The in-cycle checkConfigLineage in deploy-drift-monitor.ts is retained as a SECONDARY signal for the weaker case (config stale but still schema-valid) and is documented as such in its own header. REMAINING GAP: a hand-edit of the shared file between deploys is caught only by mechanism (2), which is operator-run, not yet on a cron.
